source.paper: Four-Coloring P6-Free Graphs. II. Finding an Excellent Precoloring

source_boundaries.meaning: definition of Q triples, admissibility, construction of P_{Q,f'}
acceptability proof and second induced-P6 contradiction
equivalence/completeness construction from a fixed extension
downstream L1/L2 construction after acceptable P' is established

audit_question: What minimal semantic information is carried by z being a common neighbor of y and y' in the rest of Lemma 11?

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11, definition of Q; printed pp. 11-12, PDF lines 1257-1300
entries.statement_before: A representative triple Q_{T,T'}=(P_{T,T'},M_{T,T'},N_{T,T'}) is selected for each relevant type pair.
entries.statement_after: The middle representative set M_{T,T'} must be contained in Y0 and complete to P_{T,T'} union N_{T,T'}; P and N are anticomplete.
entries.reason: When the three sets are singletons, membership in the original Q schema itself requires both zy and zy' edges. A two-middle SPLIT object is therefore not an instance of the original state space Q.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11, construction of S(Q), Q-admissible f', and P_{Q,f'}; printed p. 12, PDF lines 1301-1403
entries.statement_before: A valid Q satisfying CZ001 is fixed.
entries.statement_after: S(Q), Z(Q), an admissible coloring, and the normal subcase P_{Q,f'} are constructed; axioms (ii)-(iv) are restored before Lemma 10.
entries.reason: The text does not invoke the two edges zy and zy' separately here. The construction consumes Q as an already-valid representative state. Commonness enters only through CZ001. In particular, the later statement that P_{Q,f'} is a normal subcase and satisfies the cited axioms contains no new explicit joint-adjacency inference.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11 acceptability proof; printed p. 12, PDF lines 1464-1480
entries.statement_before: Separate witnesses z in N(y) intersect Y0' and z' in N(y') intersect Y0' are chosen.
entries.statement_after: Lemma 4 is invoked to assume z=z', creating one common Y0 witness.
entries.reason: This is a direct use of Lemma 4 to replace two attachments by one vertex adjacent to both y and y'. It is logically independent of the earlier definition of Q.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11 acceptability contradiction; printed p. 12, PDF lines 1481-1503
entries.statement_before: A common witness z has been obtained and z lies in Y0'.
entries.statement_after: Using z anticomplete to the stored representative triple, list/color facts, and s in T\T', the proof obtains the induced P6 z-y-s-p-m-n.
entries.reason: The displayed P6 uses zy but does not use zy' as an edge of the path. The anticompleteness of z to {p,m,n} comes from z in the residual Y0', not from joint adjacency. Thus the final contradiction has a transitive dependency on CZ003's witness identification, but no new direct need for both adjacency relations is visible in this inference.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11 equivalence/completeness proof; printed p. 12, PDF lines 1504-1527
entries.statement_before: A fixed extension c and a nonadjacent pair y in Y(T) intersect N(Y0), y' in Y(T') intersect N(Y0) with the specified colors are chosen.
entries.statement_after: Lemma 4 supplies a common neighbor z in Y0; the proof sets P={y}, M={z}, N={y'} and colors these stored vertices from c.
entries.reason: The common witness is needed so the constructed singleton triple satisfies the original CZ001 state contract M complete to P union N. This is the direct commonness dependency in the completeness direction.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11 completion of equivalence; printed pp. 12-13, PDF lines 1528-1574
entries.statement_before: All representative triples and their colors have been selected, including the CZ005 common-witness branch.
entries.statement_after: Q, S(Q), Z(Q), and P_{Q,f'} are assembled; c is shown to extend P_{Q,f'}, which was among the instances used to build M; therefore M is equivalent to P.
entries.reason: After the singleton triple has been admitted to Q, the proof does not again inspect zy and zy' jointly. Commonness is carried transitively through the fact that CZ005 produced a valid Q object and that c agrees with f' on selected vertices.

entries.location: Paper II Lemma 11 downstream L1/L2 stage; printed p. 13, PDF lines 1575-1761
entries.statement_before: An acceptable seeded precoloring P' in M is fixed.
entries.statement_after: The proof defines active colors and the L1/L2 collections and concludes equivalence using acceptability.
entries.reason: The representative triple and common vertex z are no longer referenced. The downstream proof consumes only the derived facts that P' is acceptable and belongs to an equivalent collection. Hence commonness survives only through the prior acceptability and equivalence proofs, not as a new local adjacency requirement.

derived_nodes.statement: Every seeded precoloring in M is acceptable.
M is an equivalent collection for P.
The final L1/L2 stage reaches Lemma 11 after fixing acceptable P' in M.

first_commonness_critical_inference.description: The original representative state space Q requires a singleton middle M={z} to be complete to both singleton endpoints P={y} and N={y'}.
first_commonness_critical_inference.consequence: A COMMON-to-SPLIT repair cannot be treated as a drop-in value substitution inside the existing Q schema. It would require an explicitly new state contract before any soundness/completeness proof can begin.

outcome.label: FINITE_LOCAL_COMMON_DEPENDENCIES
justification: Direct joint adjacency is concentrated in the representative-state contract CZ001, the acceptability witness collapse CZ003, and the completeness witness construction CZ005.
The acceptability P6 inference CZ004 does not visibly use the second common edge directly; it uses commonness only transitively through witness identification.
After P_{Q,f'} is constructed and M is known acceptable/equivalent, the L1/L2 stage contains no new direct reference to common z or simultaneous adjacency to y,y'.
non_claims: This does not establish that a SPLIT state exists.
This does not prove soundness or completeness of any modified Q schema.
This does not repair acceptability on P7-free graphs.
This does not lift Lemma 11 to P7-free graphs.

required_by_original_schema: one stored middle vertex in Y0
later_direct_uses: acceptability witness collapse to one Y0 vertex
completeness construction of a valid original-Q triple
minimal_information_currently_exposed.no_new_direct_use_detected_after_P_Q_fpr: The proof thereafter refers to derived acceptable/equivalent seeded precolorings rather than to the common vertex.

next_allowed_object.name: MINIMAL_SPLIT_STATE_REQUIREMENTS
next_allowed_object.required_starting_fact: Any candidate must explicitly replace the CZ001 Q-schema contract; merely storing zL,zR while pretending to remain in the old Q is invalid.
